title: Part One, Chapter 4: The Pride of Vucub-caquix

verses.t: At that time there was little light on the face of the earth, and there was not yet a sun; and then one called Vucub-caquix (that is, Seven Macaw) grew proud. There were then sky and earth, but the light of the sun and moon was clouded. And this Vucub-caquix said, "Only those few people who were drowned were like sorcerers. Now I shall be great over all the creatures. I am their sun, I am their brightness, I shall be their moon. Great is my splendour, and men shall walk and stand by me, for my eyes are of silver; they shine like precious stones, and they are green stones like the sky; my nose shines from afar like the moon, my throne is of silver, and when I come out the earth grows bright. And so I am sun and I am moon, for the light of the subjects I shall have, because my sight reaches very far." This is what that Vucub-caquix said. But Vucub-caquix was not the sun; it was his riches and his silver that made him proud. His sight reached only the place where he was, and did not reach the whole world. The face of the sun, the moon and the stars had not yet been seen, and it had not yet dawned; yet Vucub-caquix set himself up as sun and moon. The light of the sun and moon had not yet appeared; he only longed for greatness and to rise above everything. And this was at the time when the flood was made for the destruction of the men of wood. And now we shall tell how Vucub-caquix died and was defeated, and when man was made by the Creator.
